steps: 1. Standard technical analysis textbooks teach traders to wait for three higher highs and lower lows before drawi
2. Trends do not start in mid-air; they are born and propelled directly out of support and resistance price conge
3. Dynamic trendlines are constructed in real-time as price breaks out from congestion: an uptrend breakout forms
4. Every wave higher in an uptrend must be supported by rising volume, whereas counter-trend pullbacks must show
5. If a new pivot high forms at the same level as or lower than a previous pivot high, the market is stalling int
6. Coulling compares multi-timeframe analysis to driving on a three-lane highway with wing mirrors: the fast time
7. Bilateral counterparty exposure demands rigorous collateralization.
8. Always distinguish gross terminal payoff from net trading profit.
